To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) CHI is a rare but serious cause of hypoglycemic coma in the neonate and young infant.
the surgical management of CHI depends on the histologic and genetic diagnosis of the disease.

(i) preoperative imaging, pathology, and molecular biology are mandatory for the diagnosis; (ii) partial pancreatectomys are curative in focal lesions; and (iii) near-total pancreatecomy is the only curative treatment for diffuse disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a surgical approach to CHI, which is based on the histopathology of the disease.
the diagnosis and treatment of CHI in infants and children.

a better understanding of CHI and its treatment, with a view to reducing the morbidity associated with the surgical treatment of diffuse CHI and to developing a less invasive approach for the surgical treatment of focal CHI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
surgery is the treatment of choice in focal disease and a last resort option in diffuse disease.
surgery has a place in the management of CHI, but it must be performed in a specialized center and by a team of experienced surgeons.
the surgeon is an important member of the multidisciplinary management of CHI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diagnosis of focal disease must be made preoperatively and confirmed by molecular biology, and that near-total pancreatecotomy must be reserved for diffuse disease.
the surgeon has to be involved in the multidisciplinar team to diagnose the disease, to propose a treatment and to follow-up the patient.
in the management of hyperinsulinemic infants, a multidisciplinary team of endocrinologists, surgeons, radiologists, pathologists, and molecular biologists is necessary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a multidisciplinary approach is mandatory in the diagnosis and treatment of CHI.
surgery is mandatory in all focal diseases and is an option to cure diffuse disease.
the surgical management of CHI is a complex process that involves several specialists, including the surgeon.
